diagnostics.rationale: This pattern either hides diagnostics, keeps placeholder code, or duplicates a cleaner Ouro surface construct that is already active.
diagnostics.replacement: Use `[]` / `[x, y]` when the expected type is known.

diagnostics.rationale: This pattern either hides diagnostics, keeps placeholder code, or duplicates a cleaner Ouro surface construct that is already active.
diagnostics.replacement: Use `do let! x := action; ...`.
diagnostics.title: legacy do-bind syntax where let! is available

diagnostics.rationale: RETIRED. Nested-application depth is a parenthesis count, not a data-flow or pipe-equivalence proof.
diagnostics.replacement: Rule retired. Use a pipe when it clarifies flow; nesting is not a deny.
diagnostics.title: retired: deep nested application where pipe clarifies flow

diagnostics.rationale: RETIRED. `def name := other;` does not prove a pointless alias or a safe inline.
diagnostics.replacement: Rule retired. Inline or document an alias only when the wrapper is actually pointless.
diagnostics.title: retired: pointless wrapper definition

diagnostics.rationale: RETIRED. Module size is a nonblank-line count, not a mixed-responsibility proof.
diagnostics.replacement: Rule retired. Split a module when responsibility is mixed, not because a line budget fired.
diagnostics.title: retired: god module

diagnostics.rationale: RETIRED. Function size is a line-span count, not a complexity or extract-helper proof.
diagnostics.replacement: Rule retired. Extract helpers when the definition has mixed responsibility, not a span guess.
diagnostics.title: retired: too-large function

diagnostics.rationale: RETIRED. Nearby `@doc`/`docs/` text does not prove API documentation or a required export contract.
diagnostics.replacement: Rule retired. Document public APIs in the existing API/docs process, not a lexical deny.
diagnostics.title: retired: public definition without API documentation/trace

diagnostics.rationale: RETIRED. Panic/ICE grep without diagnostic-handling proof; the scanner self-hits on its own search literals.
diagnostics.replacement: Rule retired. Route failures through explicit diagnostics; a word grep is not a deny.
diagnostics.title: retired: panic/ICE-like path outside compiler diagnostic handling

diagnostics.rationale: Repeated imports add graph noise and hide dependency mistakes.
diagnostics.replacement: Remove the repeated import; one canonical `import "path.ouro";` owns the dependency edge.
diagnostics.title: duplicate import path

diagnostics.rationale: RETIRED. Style shadow scanner duplicates language lint. compiler/lint.ouro owns WShadow as OURO-LINT004.
diagnostics.replacement: Rule retired. Language lint reports accidental shadowing as OURO-LINT004.
diagnostics.title: retired: style binder or local shadowing

diagnostics.rationale: RETIRED. Style unused-binder scanner duplicates language lint. compiler/lint.ouro owns WUnused as OURO-LINT003.

diagnostics.title: retired: style unused local binding

diagnostics.rationale: Public APIs should not silently throw away constructor payloads.

diagnostics.rationale: List literals need an explicit expected `List` type to avoid hidden inference fallback.
diagnostics.replacement: Add an expected type at the binding boundary, for example `def xs : List Nat := [...]`.

diagnostics.rationale: Redundant separators are parser-permissive noise and destabilize formatter output.
diagnostics.replacement: Use one `;` separator; remove `;;` and empty declaration noise.
diagnostics.title: redundant declaration separator

diagnostics.rationale: Aliases are part of readable namespace surface and should be stable and unambiguous.
diagnostics.replacement: Use a unique PascalCase alias that does not shadow built-in names.
diagnostics.title: non-canonical import alias

diagnostics.rationale: Top-level opens leak names across a file and make imports harder to audit.
diagnostics.replacement: Use qualified references or `open Alias in expr` at the narrow expression where it is needed.
diagnostics.title: top-level open alias

profile_descriptions.baseline: safe default for external code using Ouro before opting into project policy
profile_descriptions.project: default policy for Ouro repository development
profile_descriptions.release: fail-closed profile used by CI/release gates for project-owned code
profile_descriptions.strict: maximal policy for new human-written Ouro code

profile_semantics.deny: diagnostic is an error; the gate fails
profile_semantics.forbid: diagnostic is an error and source-level suppressions are not honored
profile_semantics.warn: diagnostic is shown and recorded; build may pass
